# Fixture provenance

`reference.json` was generated by `scripts/reference.py` from checkpoint revision
`2bf128600aac4b16946f7ed8372e56117fe5e23b`, using PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU, NumPy 2.5.3,
and librosa 1.0.0. Input is 1,600 deterministic pseudo-random PCM samples; the file
records the full normalized mel features, subsampler output, final encoder output,
VAD probabilities, and empty token sequence. It contains no copied model weights.

`jfk.pcm` contains 176,000 signed little-endian 16-bit samples at 16 kHz (11 seconds),
from the public-domain JFK inaugural address. Source:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/Xenova/transformers.js-docs/resolve/main/jfk.wav
The original 44.1 kHz stereo WAV was averaged to mono, resampled with librosa's
default `soxr_hq`, and written as PCM16 with soundfile. `jfk.json` records the
independent PyTorch reference's text and all 39 token/frame/duration decisions.
The repeated “what” is present in the model output and deliberately preserved.

To reproduce the speech reference, wrap the PCM in a 16 kHz mono WAV and run:

```sh
python scripts/reference.py --audio jfk.wav --output /tmp/jfk-reference.json
```

Checkpoint tests require local model files and run only when explicitly requested.
